Keep transactions whose average is above the unweighted mean of the per-transaction averages. Show `transref`, its average, the difference from the overall mean, and the difference from the mean of the kept transactions' averages (the unweighted mean of the kept averages). Order by the difference from the kept mean, descending, NULLs last, and limit to 10. No rounding.
Same as 1, but the "overall average" is the row-level average of `anlycount` across all rows (ignoring NULLs) rather than the mean of the per-transaction averages.
Same as 1, but the "average among just the kept transactions" is the row-level average of `anlycount` across all rows belonging to the kept transactions, not the mean of the kept averages.
Same as 1, but both the overall average and the kept-group average are row-level averages (weighted by the number of rows), not means of per-transaction averages.

Transactions with no non-NULL `anlycount` have a NULL average. Under this reading, they are excluded from the overall mean and can't pass the filter, since NULL is not above anything. Alternatively, they are treated as having an average of 0 and included in the overall mean.
"How far above" is the raw difference (average minus overall average), versus a percentage or ratio above the average.

The "top 10 by that last difference" is ordered by the difference from the kept-group average. Since the kept group's average is a constant, this ordering is equivalent to ordering by the transaction's own average. Ties in the ordering are broken arbitrarily, or by `transref`.
Ties at the 10th position either cut off at exactly 10 rows, or all tied rows are included.

`transref` is the foreign key to `transactionrecord`, so grouping is by `transref` as stored in `sentimentandfundamentals`. Alternatively, it might be grouped via a join to `transactionrecord` on `transreg`, which includes only transactions that exist there.
"Don't round" means returning the full-precision values of the averages and differences, not casting to the stored `real(5,2)` or `real(7,4)` precision.

"How far above" the overall average is computed against the overall average, but "how far above the average among just the kept transactions" could be read as the kept-group average minus the transaction's average (sign reversed), instead of the transaction's average minus the kept-group average.

The "overall average of those per-transaction averages" is computed over all transactions, including those whose average is NULL, and those transactions count as 0 in the mean. This differs from reading 5, which either excludes them or treats them as 0 for the whole pipeline. Here only the denominator changes, and they are still never kept.

"Missing last" applies to a NULL difference. Under the default ordering of the target SQL dialect, NULLs may sort first or last, so an explicit NULLS LAST is needed. Under this reading the clause only affects the result if NULL differences exist.
The "top 10 by that last difference" is ordered by the difference computed from the unrounded values. Alternatively, it is ordered by the stored-precision values.
The `transref` grouping could include `sentimentandfundamentals` rows with a NULL `transref`. This is moot because `transref` is NOT NULL.
queries:
WITH per AS (
  SELECT transref, AVG(anlycount) AS avg_anly
  FROM sentimentandfundamentals
  GROUP BY transref
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_anly) AS overall_mean
  FROM per
),
kept AS (
  SELECT p.transref, p.avg_anly
  FROM per p, overall o
  WHERE p.avg_anly > o.overall_mean
),
kept_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_anly) AS km
  FROM kept
)
SELECT k.transref,
       k.avg_anly AS avg_anlycount,
       k.avg_anly - o.overall_mean AS diff_from_overall_mean,
       k.avg_anly - km.km AS diff_from_kept_mean
FROM kept k, overall o, kept_mean km
ORDER BY diff_from_kept_mean IS NULL, diff_from_kept_mean DESC
LIMIT 10;
SELECT transref, AVG(anlycount) AS avg_anlycount
FROM sentimentandfundamentals
GROUP BY transref
HAVING AVG(anlycount) > (SELECT AVG(anlycount) FROM sentimentandfundamentals);
SELECT AVG(anlycount)
FROM sentimentandfundamentals
WHERE transref IN (
  SELECT transref
  FROM sentimentandfundamentals
  GROUP BY transref
  HAVING AVG(anlycount) > (SELECT AVG(anlycount) FROM sentimentandfundamentals)
);
SELECT transref
FROM sentimentandfundamentals
GROUP BY transref
HAVING AVG(anlycount) > (SELECT AVG(anlycount) FROM sentimentandfundamentals)
